title: Evaluation harness to quantify config-induced quality drift vs latency for batch/cache policies
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Recent configuration changes to batching shape and KV cache eviction policies have shown modest latency gains in synthetic profiles but we lack systematic evidence about correlated downstream quality regressions on production slices. This ticket defines an evaluation harness and monitoring pipeline to measure 'config-induced quality drift' — the change in model output quality attributable to runtime config switches — alongside latency/throughput metrics so Product/Eng can make rollout decisions with quantified tradeoffs.

Goals:
- Provide slice-aware LQ (latency-quality) maps that show Pareto frontiers between latency metrics (P50, P95, tokens/sec) and quality metrics (LL, perplexity, automated LQ score, and human-calibrated pass rates) across batching and cache-eviction variants.
- Build a reproducible experiment harness that can run across: canary traffic, replayed production traces, and synthetic prompt suites.
- Integrate regression detection thresholds into LQ-watch alerts and generate human-review tickets for cases where quality drops exceed SLO budgets.
- Produce a compact decision table (config -> expected latency delta, expected LQ delta, and recommended rollout policy: full, canary, staggered, or rollback).

Scope & Non-Goals:
- This ticket focuses on the evaluation harness, metric definitions, and alert integration; it does not implement automatic auto-rollbacks (follow-up ticket).
- We will not change model weights or prompt templates here; only runtime config axis: microbatch size, max_batch_delay_ms, kv_cache_eviction_ttl, kv_pack_threshold, and prefix-cache modes.

Methodology:
1) Dataset & slices: use three evaluation sources in parallel: (a) a curated prompt suite of 5k prompts covering instructions, code, and multi-turn dialog with labeled gold outputs and pass/fail tests; (b) a production-replay trace sample stratified by route and customer tier (3M requests anonymized); (c) targeted difficult slices identified by the LQ-Alert history (e.g., long-context, streaming interruptions).
2) Metrics: latency: P50/P90/P95 tail, 99th-percentile token latency for streaming; throughput: avg tokens/sec and max sustained QPS. Quality: token-level log-likelihood delta, automated LQ score (ensemble of synthetic checks), BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, and a 200-sample human rated pass-rate for candidate regressions. Compute per-slice deltas vs baseline config.
3) Experiments: grid-sweep across microbatch ∈ {1,2,4,8}, max_batch_delay_ms ∈ {0,5,10,25}, kv_eviction_ttl ∈ {30s,60s,300s,inf}, kv_pack_threshold ∈ {0.5, 0.75, 0.9}. For each config, run replay and curated suite, record metrics and resource utilization. Use paired statistical tests on quality metrics to flag significant regressions (pre-registered alpha=0.01, bootstrap CI for pass-rate).
4) Ranking: compute latency-quality efficiency score per config and per-slice; produce an interactive LQ map in Console that lets product engineers filter by route, model, and SLO tier.

Instrumentation & Implementation:
- Extend the perf-harness to support replay job manifests and tie each run to a single config snapshot id.
- Emit structured experiment events to metrics pipeline (Prometheus + TSDB) with labels: config_id, slice, model, route, customer_tier.
- Add a regression-detector job that consumes daily experiment results and raises alerts when quality delta exceeds configured budgets for a slice.
- Persist experiment artifacts (raw outputs, diff reports) to GCS under experiments/runtime-config-evals/{date}/{config_id}/ for audit and human review.

Rollout & Communication: 
- Run first full sweep on a small internal canary fleet week of 2026-03-09; triage regressions and refine slices.
- Publish initial LQ-map dashboard and decision table to the Performance Guild (Confluence) and wire an on-call workflow for human verification when automated detectors fire.

Risks & Mitigations:
- False positives from flaky automated checks: mitigate with conservative thresholds and require human pass-rate confirmation before blocking rollouts.
- Privacy risk in replayed traces: use strict anonymization and customer opt-out lists; only run on infra in region X with approved access.
- Cost: full grid sweep is compute heavy; start with a reduced factorial design for non-critical routes and escalate only when slices show sensitivity.

Next steps (this ticket): scaffold harness, add experiment job templates, run reduced sweep, and integrate alerting. Follow-on tickets will automate daily sweeps and UI improvements for the LQ map.
acceptance_criteria: Perf harness can execute a replay manifest and attach a unique config_id to all outputs.
Automated pipeline computes per-slice latency (P50/P95) and quality deltas for each config and stores them in TSDB/BigQuery for dashboards.
Regression-detector emits alerts to #lq-watch when quality delta (pass-rate or LQ-score) exceeds configured slice budget and marks candidate regressions with links to artifacts.
A first reduced grid-sweep (at least 12 config points) completed on replay and curated suite with preliminary LQ maps published in Console.
Decision table summarizing recommended rollout policy for top 8 configs is created and reviewed by PM and Core Runtime lead.
